idiom_name: container/heap pending set under sync.Mutex + time.Timer gap deadline
implementation_notes: Go's standard library supplies the parts - container/heap (or a sorted slice) for the pending window, sync.Mutex for the cursor, time.Timer/time.AfterFunc for the gap deadline and a channel for order-preserving delivery - but the resequencer itself is hand-written; there is no stdlib or de-facto framework resequencer. A common shape is one goroutine owning the window and receiving on a channel, which removes the mutex entirely and turns the gap policy into a select over the inbound channel and the timer's channel. When the disorder comes from partitioning, fixing the key choice (one partition or consumer per ordering key) is cheaper than buffering.
pitfalls: A gap deadline driven by a time.Timer must be re-armed on delivery, otherwise the first timeout keeps firing and skips holes that no longer exist.
container/heap requires the receiver's element access (pending[0]) to work on the heap type itself; sharing a []Msg slice with a copy makes Push/Pop mutate the wrong backing array.
Delivering the returned slice after unlocking is safe only while the consumer preserves order; a worker pool downstream of the resequencer reintroduces the scramble.
